docs.title: Entities

docs.text: Diffusion features parallax-corrected cubemaps. To place one, create a brush entity named cubemap_box . Creating the entity You can create it both with origin-brush and without. Origin-brush (a brush with ORIGIN texture) represents a view point, where a cubemap would photograph the world from, in game. Without the origin-brush, center of the cubemap_box entity will be used. Important: When making cubemap_box with an origin-brush, it is crucial to select the origin-brush first, then the cubemap brush itself, and only then press Tie to entity . This is related to how brushes are being written into a map file. If you select the origin-brush last, the correct origin won't be saved. Texture that is applied to a cubemap brush is not important, but for the sake of visibility I use TOOLSCUBEMAP texture in diffusion.wad. Entity parameters cubemapsize - deprecated, does nothing. By default, the cubemap is created in the best quality already. rendermode - editor only . Sets the brush to transparent mode in the editor, for better visiblity. renderamt - editor only . The amount of brush transparency in the editor, for better visibility. Applying a cubemap to brush faces The logic is very simple - if a brush face, particularly a center of a surface after map compilation is inside of the cubemap volume, this surface will receive this cubemap. If a surface is inside multiple cubemap volumes, the smallest cubemap volume will be used. Same logic applies for models, but it's worth to note that models choose their cubemaps using their entity origin. Example: a house in the middle of a field. Placing one huge cubemap around the map will apply this cubemap to everything - both inside and outside walls of the house, and the field. Now place smaller cubemaps inside the house to replace the outside cubemap with the internal ones. Note The texture material file must have the parameter ReflectScale (0.0 - 1.0) for a cubemap to work. You can also adjust cubemap quality using lower resolution mip level of the cubemap image, by using ReflectLod (0 - highest quality. The higher the number, the worse the quality). Building cubemaps Load the map in game. Enable cheats using sv_cheats 1 Disable culling for certain models and brushes by typing sv_cubemap_culling 1 Type buildcubemaps and wait for the cubemaps to build (left bottom corner of the screen) When done with cubemap building, revert sv_cubemap_culling back to 0. Optimizing disk space By default, each cubemap is saved as 6 TGA files, which can take a lot of disk space as well as GPU memory. It is recommended to convert them to a single DDS file, which can be easily done using Xash3D DDS cubemap creator - an automated tool that I created for personal use. Once DDS files are created, you can delete all TGA files. Now each cubemap will take only 1 Mb of space.

docs.text: A few example maps to help you learn level creation for Diffusion. Chapter 2 Desert The middle section of Chapter 2. The biggest map Diffusion has to offer, although not the most detailed. This map has land vehicles, such as the Buggy, Hummer, Cybertruck, Jeep, and water vehicle such as the Jetski. The map has dynamic weather change mechanic - sandstorm. Download MAP | Download JMF (last updated: 29 Apr 2026) dm_test A multiplayer map which has practically everything that Diffusion has to offer. The map features dynamic weather mechanic (heavy rain), an APC vehicle and a semi-cut Shield mechanic, which was supposed to be featured in the campaign but was cut very late in development. The shield code is still there, so it has been repurposed for multiplayer. Download MAP | Download JMF (last updated 29 Apr 2026) Chapter 4 Mega City - Crystal Tech HQ The last map of Chapter 4. This map features the Drone Shop and the drone introduction. Download MAP | Download JMF (last updated 29 Apr 2026)

docs.text: Mapping setup To make maps for Diffusion, I used J.A.C.K. editor. Other editors like Trenchbroom or Valve Hammer Editor were not tested. You can get free version of J.A.C.K. here or Steam version (paid) here . It is recommended to use Steam version as it updates more often, but the free one should work just fine. FGD file You need this entity description file to use in the editor. Download FGD Map compilers For Diffusion I use edited compilers from PrimeXT A few minor changes were done to them - for example handling of the Diffusion-specific cubemaps, so it is important that you use these compilers and not from original PrimeXT (my fork of PrimeXT here ) The file below includes 4 exe files - csg, bsp, vis and rad. You must set them up in the editor. Download map compilers Compiling the map Press F9 in J.A.C.K. and "Run Map" window will open. Switch to Expert mode. In VIS parameters, specify -threads parameter to specify the amount of CPU threads that will be used for compilation. It is recommended to set the number of threads less than what you have in total, so you'll have one or two free threads for basic tasks while you wait for the map to compile. In RAD parameters, you can specify the ones below. These were used to compile all Diffusion maps. You can tune them to your liking if you know what you're doing. Otherwise I recommend to just use these. Also don't forget to add -threads here as well. -smooth 45 -bounce 32 -blur 2 -accurate_trans -envsky -studiobounce 4 -sky 0.425 -texchop 64 Here's an example how it looks in my editor.
docs.title: Setup
